title: Runtime SkinnedMeshRenderer adapter for resolved creature geometry
description:
## Summary
Create a real runtime Unity `SkinnedMeshRenderer` adapter that installs already-authored binding data + the `CreatureRig` indexed bone hierarchy into Unity, producing the MVP's generated creature rendered through a `SkinnedMeshRenderer`.

## Scope
- A separate presentation adapter (NOT inside `CreatureRig`, NOT in the pure generation path). It consumes binding data (per-item weights from 0130/0131) + `CreatureRig`'s index-parallel `Transform[]` and builds once: `Mesh.boneWeights`/`BoneWeight` (cap 4, reuse `MaxBoneInfluencesPerVertex`), `Mesh.bindposes` (full `Matrix4x4` inverse-rest-bone-in-mesh-local; bind==rest convention), and a `SkinnedMeshRenderer` with `.bones`/`.rootBone` from `CreatureRig`. Preserve submeshes/materials (MaterialRegion/ADR-009).
- Lock the shared `SkeletonSnapshot.Capture` bone-index ordering invariant with 0130/0131; mesh-local==creature-space==rig-host-space at identity; mirrored bone handling via `SemanticBoneResolver`/`MirrorUtility`.
- `GeneratedCreature` stays pose-free; adapter is a pure data→Unity-Mesh converter (no re-derivation of weights/bindposes). Animation ticks only change bone Transform position/rotation; no mesh.SetVertices/RecalculateNormals/Bounds, no weight/bindpose/rebind rebuild per frame.
- Keep `LinearBlendSkinning.Deform` as the cross-check oracle, not a per-frame runtime path.
- Adapter must remain compatible with the generalized rig contract: arbitrary numbers of limbs, authored order, supported limb types, and arbitrary Body attachment positions must flow through the same index/identity binding path without biped/quadruped-specific logic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- SMR rest result == generated rest geometry within tolerance; one posed bone deforms expected vertices; posed→rest restores within tolerance.
- Posed SMR == `LinearBlendSkinning.Deform` oracle within tolerance on the same real geometry (the test that proves Unity wiring, not just the math).
- Mirror: mirrored deformation == reflection of unmirrored via `MirrorUtility`.
- Renderer setup happens once; per-frame changes transforms only; no per-frame managed allocations or mesh rebuild (minimal zero-alloc ceiling embedded as acceptance).
- Ownership/lifecycle: rebuild/destroy/rebind leaves no orphaned generated objects; source mesh not modified.
- Skinning mesh preserves the source `Mesh.indexFormat` as well as geometry/submesh structure, so large generated meshes retain their valid index width.

## Validation
PLAY MODE REQUIRED (hard gate): `SkinnedMeshRenderer`/`Mesh.boneWeights`/`bindposes`/`bones`/`rootBone` are Engine types readable only in a running instance. Rest, posed, restore, mirror, and lifecycle tests in PlayMode on a real `GeneratedCreature`; plus dotnet builds and git diff --check. Cannot be marked Done without Unity validation.

## Current status
Done. Prior focused Unity validation recorded 13/13 binding/renderer tests and full 610/610 Runtime PlayMode with zero managed allocation for 1,000 ApplyPose calls. Later source hardening preserves the established adapter contract, including source mesh index-format preservation, and now also makes replacement binding transactional so a failed replacement cannot destroy the previous valid presentation. No new Unity completion claim is made for this follow-up hardening pass.

## Residuals
Strict full-SMR reflected-mesh equality remains covered indirectly by the pure LBS/mirror layer plus a real mirrored-limb SMR-vs-LBS test. TSK-0130 rigid mesh-asset weighting and TSK-0134 runtime performance benchmarking remain separate scopes.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Sprint round started. Consuming TSK-0131 in-worktree ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring (bind-index = SkeletonSnapshot.Capture order). Design: pure SkinnedMeshBindingBuilder (bindposes = TRS(rest.Pos,rest.Rot,one).inverse, bind==rest; BoneWeight cap 4) + thin runtime MonoBehaviour CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer that clones the source implicit-surface mesh (never mutates it), sets boneWeights/bindposes, and attaches a SkinnedMeshRenderer with .bones = CreatureRig indexed bones + rootBone = first root bone. Mesh-local == creature-space == rig-host-space at identity. Per-frame = rig.ApplyPose only (zero alloc, no mesh rebuild). LBS.Deform remains the oracle only.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Sprint round implementation + validation evidence (TSK-0132). New SkinnedMeshBindingBuilder and CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer were implemented as a separate presentation adapter; focused 13/13 and full Runtime 610/610 PlayMode evidence was recorded, including zero managed allocation across 1,000 ApplyPose calls. Residual risk accepted: strict pointwise reflected full-SMR equality is not directly asserted.

comments.body: Sprint R4 orchestrator review: independently re-ran focused CreatureSkinnedMeshRendererTests 7/7 passed. Adapter separation, ownership/lifecycle, bind-index contract, rest/posed/oracle/mirror coverage, and zero-allocation ApplyPose evidence were accepted. Parent TSK-0077 stays open for broader geometry-binding work.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Bug fix evidence (2026-09-07): dinus_uprightus preview failed because the implicit welded SDF includes non-limb parts whose inferred bones are attachment points (HasSegment=false), so no segment influence was eligible for some vertices. Added BuildBindingInfluences to preserve segment influences and add deterministic zero-length point influences for attachment bones; CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer now uses it. Added regression coverage in ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoringTests. Validation: ProceduralCreature.Runtime and ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime dotnet builds passed; git diff --check passed; focused PlayMode test BuildBindingInfluences_IncludesAttachmentBonesAsPointInfluences passed 1/1. Full runtime suite still has unrelated pre-existing topology/SMR and single-root fixture failures.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Sequential code-health hardening: `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.BuildSkinningMeshCopy` now preserves the source mesh `indexFormat`, preventing the bind-time copy from silently narrowing large generated meshes to the default index width. This is a source-level compatibility fix only; the existing Unity validation evidence for the adapter remains the authoritative completion gate.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Code-health hardening: `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.Bind` now builds the replacement mesh/GameObject/SkinnedMeshRenderer completely before clearing the previous valid bind. Failed replacement construction cleans up only the uncommitted replacement, including its generated Mesh. This protects live preview rebinds without adding work to the animation tick.
